title: Transport for NSW launches the PAWS AI animal-detection and smart-signage trial on the Monaro Highway between Bredbo and Williamsdale; no outcome yet
summary: Transport for NSW announced a trial of its Protective Animal Warning System, in which two AI-enabled cameras on the Monaro Highway would trigger driver warnings; no results are reported.
account: The New South Wales (NSW) Government announced its Protective Animal Warning System trial on 18 July 2026. The trial grew out of a 2024 Wildlife Symposium recommendation and an initial A$500,000 government commitment. Transport for NSW developed the system, which uses thermal and optical cameras with AI to recognize wildlife and trigger roadside warnings. The announcement describes training at Yennora and Symbio Wildlife Park before a live trial on the Monaro Highway. About Regional's separate interviews add the planned two-camera layout on a 13 km stretch between Bredbo and Williamsdale and the role of local wildlife carers. The intended benefit is fewer collisions after drivers receive warnings. Transport for NSW plans to monitor the speed of vehicles approaching the signs. Wildlife carers have been asked to move dead animals to the roadside so that strikes can be counted. Neither source reports a measured change in detection accuracy, driver behavior or collisions. As of 29 October 2026 no results have been reported.
purpose: Detect wildlife near the road and warn drivers dynamically to limit wildlife-vehicle strikes; no benefit has yet been observed.
